top_signal.title: My 50/50 business partner keeps trying to change our profit split after the work is done. Would you leave this partnership?
top_signal.summary: I’m looking for outside perspective because I’m at the point where I don’t know if these are normal business disagreements or if I need to start planning my exit.  My business partner and I went into real estate investing together with the understanding that we were 50/50 partners. We both take financial risk, we both work, and we split the profits 50/50.  On our first flip, after we had already purchased the property and I was financially committed, she asked me to take only 25% of the profit even though I was still taking on 50% of the financial risk. Her reasoning was that she had more experience and would be mentoring me through the first project. I agreed because I was new and trusted her.  The problem is that the project ended up going significantly over budget, and a lot of the things I thought her experience would protect us from didn’t happen.  She underestimated how much money we needed from our lender, and she handled most of the contractor relationship. We didn’t have strong enough contracts/change-order procedures in place, and our contractor eventually presented us with costs dramatically higher than the original bid. We’re now potentially out a substantial amount of money that I never anticipated when I agreed to the deal.  I’m not saying every cost overrun is her fault.
